status: declared before outcomes; queued behind live full QA
question: Are learned full-photo crop failures driven mainly by background leakage, missed paper, or remaining localization/outline assumptions?
scope: Twenty-two previously inspected development photographs. Annotation-assisted diagnostic, not trained prediction or reconstruction accuracy.

arms.unchanged: Frozen RGB-calibrated material and original predicted body.
arms.known-background: Set body probability to zero only at independently annotated background pixels.
arms.known-paper: Set body probability to one only at independently annotated paper pixels.
arms.known-body: Apply both known-background and known-paper interventions.

invariants: Unknown body pixels retain their original probabilities.
Every material probability is byte-identical across arms.
Full photographs, source windows and locator geometry/support thresholds are fixed.
No rough ROI, supplied corner, template fitting or retraining.
Rotate arm order for every photograph.
evaluation: Compare crop proposal availability against the unchanged arm, including gains and losses by source.
Inspect returned and rejected quadrilaterals against source photographs; proposal count alone does not establish correct cropping.
Inspect support diagnostics to distinguish missing lower edges, lobe failures, and cap-colour failures.
Do not interpret failure under partial annotations as failure with a perfect silhouette; unlabelled contour pixels remain predicted.
